summary: Australian music industry figure Ian Molly Meldrum has died in Melbourne at age 83 following a long illness. In the United Kingdom, police evacuated the Co-op Live arena in Manchester after an unknown substance was released among the crowd at a concert. The Indonesian government announced the commencement of civil servant recruitment for 167,113 positions starting November 27. Meanwhile, the Department of the Army in the United States prepared to detonate five tons of unstable, toxic explosives at an Iowa munitions plant. Additionally, Indonesian authorities held an ethics hearing regarding the 2024 presidential candidacy process.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India initiated nationwide water testing following legal action regarding a Bisleri product sample. In Indonesia, authorities recovered 24 bodies at a factory site in Cikande while searching for 30 missing individuals, and National Police Chief General Suyudi Ario Seto reassigned 704 police officers. Drones struck Khartoum in Sudan, damaging residential areas and a United Nations building. Additionally, the Democratic Party secured a majority in the United States House of Representatives, and Rafael Nadal was appointed to the Real Madrid board of directors following an Extraordinary General Assembly election.

Russian military assets in Libya and the Baltic Sea sustained damage following drone attacks, while Indonesia and the European Union signed a comprehensive trade and investment agreement. In Brazil, former President Jair Bolsonaro remains in intensive care due to an abdominal obstruction, and the government declared a state of public calamity in Tupanciretã following severe storms. Meanwhile, a boat accident in Nigeria resulted in 24 deaths, and the Mexican military captured a leader of the Beltran Leyva gang. These events reflect a day of significant governmental, economic, and security developments occurring across diverse international regions.

A security guard and a mob targeted a police vehicle in the Pantai Indah Kapuk area of Indonesia following a false hit-and-run accusation. In other developments, the Ministry of Home Affairs in Indonesia recognized regional governments for administrative performance. The United Kingdom and the European Union finalized a framework agreement to reset relations following post-Brexit tensions. In Simalungun, Indonesia, a collision between a train and a minibus resulted in one death and three injuries, while two men died after a microlight glider crashed into Loch Leven in Scotland.

Boca Juniors secured the 2026 Copa Sudamericana title in Colombia after defeating Atletico-MG. In Indonesia, provincial governments finalized 2027 minimum wage increases across several regions, while Defense Minister Sjafrie Sjamsoeddin met with officials to discuss revisions to national defense law. In the United States, shares of Anthropic declined during a broader technology market sell-off, and Elon Musk commented on his midterm election campaign spending. Additionally, the Danish parliament approved a tripartite security agreement with Greenland and the United States, and Russian authorities reported a renewed attack on the Crimean Bridge.

Hakeem Jeffries received the formal nomination from House Democrats to serve as the Speaker of the House in the United States, alongside intelligence reports predicting continued technical infrastructure outages. In Indonesia, the National Police Chief reported the seizure of narcotics, a fatal explosion occurred at an oil refinery in Blora, and Bank Indonesia raised benchmark interest rates to manage currency fluctuations. Meanwhile, Israeli military forces conducted a ground operation in the central Gaza Strip, and Cricket Australia organized a new forum to address the 2018 ball-tampering incident following renewed public allegations from player Cameron Bancroft.

The Indonesian U-17 football team advanced to the 2027 AFC Asian Cup, marking a milestone for Southeast Asian sports. Meanwhile, a magnitude 7.2 earthquake occurred in the Maluku Barat Daya region of Indonesia, though officials confirmed no tsunami risk. In the United States, significant banking service outages impacted users at major financial institutions, while the National Security Agency reported temporary downtime on a classified network. Internationally, diplomats at the APEC and ASEAN summits addressed maritime negotiations and bilateral relations, as reports emerged regarding a potential security threat involving Iran and the United States administration.

Theresa May has advised Prime Minister Andy Burnham to accept the outcome of Brexit in the United Kingdom following a bilateral agreement with the European Union. In Indonesia, the MPR is reviewing Mahfud MD's concerns regarding the vice president election date, while provincial governments are announcing new minimum wage figures for 2027. Meanwhile, Ukrainian forces have targeted the Kerch Bridge using drone and missile strikes. In France, the FIFA presidential election features Gianni Infantino, Philippe Diallo, and Tashima as candidates. Additionally, President Donald Trump has proposed a potential meeting with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during the APEC summit in China.

A drone strike attributed to Iran hit a civilian industrial facility and targeted two tankers in Bahrain, resulting in two injuries. In political developments, the Samajwadi Party and Congress began seat-sharing negotiations in India, while South Korean Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned following exam-related controversies. Authorities captured cartel figure Fausto Isidro Meza Flores in Mexico during an operation that caused 11 deaths. Furthermore, the United States lost its measles-elimination status as cases reached the highest levels since 1991, and Estonia announced the closure of all Russian border crossings following an attempted arson attack on a drone factory.

The United States Department of Justice is moving to dismiss a legal challenge regarding the Alaska Senate race while federal officials report that aging infrastructure caused a national aviation shutdown. In Indonesia, Gibran Rakabuming Raka has formally resigned as Vice President, and police have searched the Kupang Regent's residence as part of a criminal investigation. Meanwhile, the Bharatiya Janata Party has criticized Rahul Gandhi's recent social media activity and political statements in India. In Australia, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Minister Chris Bowen are facing backlash following the failure to reach an agreement at the COP31 climate summit.

President Prabowo Subianto met with South Korean President Lee Jae Myung at the ASEAN Summit to coordinate the upcoming broadcast of a BTS concert in Jakarta. Domestically, Indonesia faces a state budget deficit of Rp379 trillion, investigations into a trafficking syndicate sending nationals to fight in Russia, and ongoing discussions regarding a successor for the vice presidency. Internationally, Australia concluded its aerial firefighting mission in East Kalimantan, while in India, Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed past gold purchasing policies, and a Pakistani minister attended a forum in New Delhi despite regional political tensions.

President Prabowo Subianto prepares to submit two vice presidential candidates to the Indonesian MPR, following political scrutiny regarding the resignation of Gibran Rakabuming Raka. In the United States, Democrat Scott Colom secured a historic win in the Mississippi Senate election, while authorities identified a suspect in a fatal Washington DC shooting and former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang indicated availability to return to his previous role. Additionally, Australian search teams successfully located a missing teenager after a six-day rescue operation in the wilderness. Indonesian authorities continue efforts to address government reform and legal accountability for corruption and fraud.

Jakarta authorities are addressing recurring landslides in South Jakarta by planning permanent retaining walls and deploying emergency response teams to assist displaced residents. In the United Kingdom, Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino oversaw a 4-0 defeat against Liverpool following an early red card. The Philippines hosted the 49th ASEAN summit, where leaders discussed regional cooperation, while Spain experienced its first general strike in fourteen years as protesters demanded government action on housing and living costs. Meanwhile, Italy initiated mass school evacuations due to widespread bomb hoaxes, which Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni later confirmed posed no concrete threat to public safety.
